paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, and I'll say so once. Isaiah 13 is a burden against Babylon, the jewel of the kingdoms, and it says the LORD of Hosts is the One mobilizing the army (Isaiah 13:4). The proud city looked untouchable, and God says He will "end the haughtiness of the arrogant and lay low the pride of the ruthless" (Isaiah 13:11). The big lesson is that no power, no wall and no pile of gold sits above God.

So here's why it matters to you: Babylon was called "the glory of the pride of the Chaldeans" (Isaiah 13:19), and still her days would not be prolonged (Isaiah 13:22). Anything we lean on instead of God, whether it's a paycheck, a title or a spotless reputation, is built on ground that can be shaken. I think the passage is asking you a quiet question: what are you holding up as your jewel? I spent years in a junk drawer, and I can tell you the only thing that stayed solid back there was God.

One more thing, baker, because this burden says the Day of the LORD is coming (Isaiah 13:9), and that's the reason my ovens stay ready. I don't know when it comes, and neither do you (Matthew 24:36). So we stay ready, we stay humble and we keep our eyes on the One who holds every kingdom.
